requirements.title: Upper-Division Writing Requirement

rules.manualCheck: Co-register for BIO 459 with BIO 365 or an approved alternate advanced course in the same term. A BIO 365 lab report or term paper from the alternate course must be submitted to BIO 459 Brightspace Assignments and pass Program in Writing and Rhetoric review before the end of the term.

requirements.sourceText: To satisfy the Upper-Division Writing requirement for the major in Biochemistry, students must co-register for the 0-credit BIO 459 course with either BIO 365 (Biochemistry lab) or an alternate approved advanced course in biological sciences or chemistry (see below). Students MUST enroll in BIO 459 at the same time they are registering for the respective advanced course. To receive WRTD credit and a satisfactory grade in BIO 459, either a BIO 365 lab report or term paper from another approved advanced biology/chemistry course must be submitted for writing evaluation prior to the end of the term and pass the review process.

policies.sourceText: All courses offered for the major must be taken for a letter grade.

A minimum grade of C must be obtained in fulfilling all biochemistry major requirements in: Foundational Courses in Related Fields, Foundational Courses in Biology, Advanced Courses in Biology, and Advanced Biology/Chemistry electives (see below).
Among these requirements, Biochemistry I and II (BIO 361 and BIO 362) and a minimum of nine credits of additional advanced biology courses must be completed at Stony Brook University.

Among these requirements, Biochemistry I and II (BIO 361 and BIO 362) and a minimum of nine credits of additional advanced biology courses must be completed at Stony Brook University. These advanced courses in biology include BIO 310, BIO 320 (or other approved Genetics), BIO 365, or approved "Advanced Biology/Chemistry elective" courses (see below).

fulfillment.sourceText: Satisfactory completion of BIO 459 will fulfill the Stony Brook Curriculum (SBC) "Writing in the Discipline" WRTD learning objectives.

notes.text: Contact the Biochemistry Director of Undergraduate Studies (Bernadette Holdener, biochem_ugpd@stonybrook.edu) for course combinations and approvals. Students may not declare a double major among biochemistry, biology, or pharmacology majors. Double majors or minors with Chemistry, Bioengineering, Marine Sciences, or Marine Vertebrate Biology should consult the Biochemistry director and the second program's director.
The major requires approximately 69 to 74 credits. Biochemistry I and II (BIO 361 and BIO 362) must be taken at Stony Brook, along with at least nine credits of additional advanced biology courses.
Prerequisite grades: a grade of C or higher in BIO 202, CHE 321 & CHE 322 or CHE 331 & CHE 332 is required to enroll in BIO 361 and BIO 362. BIO 361 must be taken before BIO 362.
CHE 301 has additional pre/co-requisites: MAT 203 or MAT 211 or AMS 210 or AMS 261; PHY 125, PHY 131/PHY 133, or PHY 141. CHE 312 is recommended for biochemistry majors.
Students who do not place into MAT 125 or MAT 131 on the math placement examination must complete MAT 123 (or MAT 119/MAT 123) as a required course for the major.

Alternate approved advanced courses for the writing requirement (co-registered with BIO 459) are: BIO 312, BIO 320, BIO 321, BIO 327, BIO 335, BIO 336, BIO 344, BIO 352, BIO 353, BIO 354, BIO 364, BIO 365, BIO 366, BIO 367, BIO 385, BIO 386, 400-level BIO or CHE readings or research courses with instructor permission, and EBH 302. Enrollment in upper-division labs other than BIO 365 is limited.

Biochemistry Honors requires a cumulative GPA of at least 3.50 in all courses required for the major and an acceptable thesis based on a laboratory research project. Students must contact the Biochemistry Honors Coordinator (Benjamin Martin) no later than the second week of classes in their last semester.
Accelerated programs not evaluated here: the 5-year BS/MS in Biochemistry and Cell Biology, the BS/MS in Chemistry, and the BS/MBA options.
Calculus requirement can also be met by level 9 on the mathematics placement examination (not verifiable from a transcript; confirm with an advisor).
